articles.title: From stage 6 onwards, Pogacar 'never let go' during Tour de France
articles.summary: Tadej Pogacar won a record-equaling fifth Tour de France title on Sunday. The 27-year-old Slovenian dominated this year's race to join Belgian Eddy Merckx, Spaniard Miguel Indurain and Frenchmen Jacques Anquetil and Bernard Hinault as the only riders to win five Tours. "From stage 6 onwards, he never let go," said James Vasina, FRANCE 24 journalist reporting from the finish line in Paris.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Wildfires in France: French farmers provide water tankers to help fight fire
articles.summary: "Civilian farmers are trying to help firefighters by bringing in tankers of water to keep their hoses running," FRANCE 24 reporter Luke Shrago said, reporting from Lège-Cap-Ferret, where one of the largest forest fires France has seen since WWII is still blazing.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Germany: Berlin Pride attack believed to be an act of Islamic extremist terror
articles.summary: German investigators on Sunday searched for a man who allegedly drove a van into a crowd near Berlin's Pride festival, killing one person and injuring many others, before allegedly stabbing additional people with a machete in what authorities believe was an Islamist extremist terror attack.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.summary: Andrew Hilliar has more.

articles.summary: FRANCE 24 report by Gulliver Cragg.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: The week in pictures: Wildfires rage in Europe, youth protests rock India and UK names new PM
articles.summary: Unprecedented wildfires swept across France and Spain, youth-led protests in India forced the country's education minister to resign and Andy Burnham became the United Kingdom's new prime minister. FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro launches Brazil presidential campaign, touts support from Milei
articles.summary: Brazilian Senator Flavio Bolsonaro, eldest son of former president Jair Bolsonaro, on Saturday formally launched his bid to challenge President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in October's election, showcasing support from Argentine President Javier Milei, an AI-generated message from his jailed father and a ‌video address from Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Football: WAFCON kicks off in Morocco with record 16-nation line-up
articles.summary: Thando Sibiya, Sports Presenter and Journalist, is our guest.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: ‘Bullied, beaten up, killed’: Armenia's drag queens risk it all for the stage
articles.summary: Armenian attitudes toward the LGBTQ community have transformed in recent years, in part due to the war in Ukraine. While a queer club in Yerevan was firebombed in 2012, the capital is now home to a thriving underground drag scene. But despite these events attracting hundreds, police raids and family rejection are still commonplace.
articles.author: Kal BERJIKIAN

articles.title: Deadly attack on holiday camp in Russian-held part of Ukraine, officials say
articles.summary: At least 11 people were killed, including five children, in an overnight drone attack on a holiday camp in a Russian-held part of Ukraine's ‌Zaporizhzhia region, Russian installed local authorities said on Saturday, ⁠accusing Ukraine of deliberately attacking civilians.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Wildfires ravage southwest France: Thousands face devastation after evacuation
articles.summary: A raging wildfire in southwest France forced the evacuation of 55,000 people overnight Sunday, bringing the total forced out of their homes to 220,000 in one region alone, as flames crept ever closer to the wine region city of Bordeaux. Authorities in France's Gironde region, where Bordeaux is located, issued overnight evacuation orders for five more localities southwest of the historic city, as shifting, gusting winds and arid conditions complicated the massive effort to limit the spread of the monster blaze that has burned out of control since midweek
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Romanian jet shoots down drone entering country's airspace for third day in a row
articles.summary: A Romanian fighter jet on Sunday shot down the third drone flying into the country's airspace in as many days, the defence minister said. A government investigation reportedly identified the first of the three drones as a Shahed model used by Russia in its war with Ukraine.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: France fire situation 'remains very unfavourable' says interior minister
articles.summary: French Interior Minister Laurent Nunez said on Sunday the wildfire situation in southwestern France was "very unfavourable"."Another difficult night on the wildfire front," Nunez said on X. A total of 2,500 firefighters, including a Swiss firefighting team, 1,500 military personnel and around 1,200 police have been deployed to battle the blazes in the southwestern department of Gironde, he said.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: German police hunt suspect in Berlin Pride attack: 1 dead and 16 injured
articles.summary: German authorities on Sunday issued a wanted notice for a fugitive suspect in the van rammingnear Berlin’s Pride festival that left one person dead and injured at least 16 others.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Israel detains over 70 suspects following deadly violence in the West Bank
articles.summary: Israel’s military said it detained over 70 suspects across the occupied West Bank overnight and on Saturday, a day after troops deployed across the territory following violence that left two Isrelisoldiers and four Palestinian villagers dead. Soldiers remained in the village of Tell, in the northern West Bank, where Friday's clashes were centered. Palestinians described searches that included raids of a hospital in the city of Nablus, one of the territory's most violent areas.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Women's Football: Women's Africa Cup of Nations kicks off in Morocco
articles.summary: The 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations (WAFCON) kicks off in Morocco on Sunday with qualification for the World Cup and a record two-million-dollar first prize on the line. A record 16-nation line-up -- up from 12 at the previous edition -- will compete with 10-time title-holders and defending champions Nigeria the team to beat.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Women's AFCON 2026: Tournament gets underway after months of delay
articles.summary: Originally scheduled for last spring, the 2026 Women's Africa Cup of Nations finally kicks off this Sunday in Rabat, Morocco. Algeria take on Senegal in the opening match, while defending champions Nigeria begin their quest to retain the title as the tournament favourites.
articles.author: L'Equipe TV

articles.title: Wildfires keep southwest France on edge: Evacuations top 200,000
articles.summary: FRANCE 24 reporter Luke Shrago has more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: In pictures: Wildfires ravage parts of southern France
articles.summary: Thousands of people were evacuated in southwest France on Thursday, as a wildfire ravaged a seaside pine forest. Hundreds of firefighters were battling the fire, which started around midday on Wednesday. FRANCE 24 looks at some of the most striking images of the fire.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Controversial West African activist Kemi Seba detained in Paris
articles.summary: Kemi Seba, a controversial African activist known for his virulent anti-Western stance, has been arrested in Paris, a source close to the case told AFP Tuesday.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: France’s new health pass rules raise questions as many scramble to adapt
articles.summary: While the extension of France’s health pass and other new anti-Covid 19 measures announced by President Emmanuel Macron Monday night are yet to be hammered out in detail, what’s certain is that a full-throttled return to a normal life of frequenting café terraces, restaurants, cinemas, theatres and other culture and leisure activities will now hinge on having a pass sanitaire (or health pass).
articles.author: Romain BRUNET

articles.title: Daughter loses legal case in bitter Asterix family feud
articles.summary: A long-running family feud between Asterix co-creator Albert Uderzo and his daughter took a new twist on Tuesday after judges dismissed a claim by Sylvie Uderzo that her father was mentally frail and being exploited.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Thousands of tourists forced to evacuate as fire rages in southwest France
articles.summary: More than 20,000 people, most of them tourists, on Thursday were evacuated as a wildfire ravaged a forest in Le Porge, southwest France. The fire started midday on Wednesday and hundreds of firefighters have been deployed to the region. France has experienced three heatwaves since May, fuelling wildfires.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Top contemporary French artist Christian Boltanski dies aged 76
articles.summary: Christian Boltanski, one of France's top contemporary artists whose multimedia works probed the meaning of mortality and memory, has died aged 76, a former museum director told AFP on Sunday.
articles.author: NEWS WIRES

articles.title: French environment minister to stay in post amid 'urgency' to act on climate
articles.summary: France's environment minister Monique Barbut said Wednesday that she will remain in her post despite her disagreement with a bill on bee-harming pesticides, given the "urgency" to act on climate change. Earlier in the day, Barbut said she would submit her resignation to the president.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Louvre gallery where jewellery heist took place to reopen to public
articles.summary: The Apollo Gallery at Paris's Louvre Museum, the site of the jewelry heist of October 2025, is set to reopen to the public on Wednesday without any jewelry on display.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: France's National Rally targeted as part of Europe-wide raids over alleged far-right embezzlement
articles.summary: France's National Rally was on Tuesday targeted as part of Europe-wide raids following suspicions of the misappropriation of European funds by the now-defunct Identity and Democracy (ID) group of MEPs, the European Public Prosecutor’s Office (EPPO) said, onfirming a report in French daily Le Monde.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: How the French army trains for 'high-intensity' combat
articles.summary: France's new military programming law increases the country's defence budget to 2 percent of GDP by 2025. It's an investment in the modernisation of equipment, but also in the training of soldiers. The aim is to teach soldiers to face an army at least as well equipped as that of France in a context of global rearmament. Our reporters Fadile Bhayat, Mandi Heshmati and Caroline Grandjean followed French troops during a "high-intensity" training exercise.
articles.author: Fadile BHAYAT

articles.title: France explored Pegasus spyware deal despite Morocco espionage claims
articles.summary: France briefly explored acquiring the controversial Pegasus spyware in 2019, according to media investigations, even as Morocco was allegedly using the Israeli-made surveillance tool to target French ministers. The report claims President Emmanuel Macron ultimately rejected the purchase to avoid reliance on foreign technology. Morocco has denied the spying allegations.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: 'A lot of French politicians are out of touch with a large part of the population'
articles.summary: Our guest is Fabien Truong, a sociologist, author and associate professor at the University of Paris. A former schoolteacher, he spent a decade following the lives of around 20 of his students, charting their progress from the time they took their end of school exams to when they finished their higher education. Those 10 years took in the riots that rocked France back in 2005 to the terror attacks of January 2015. He gives us his take on the French presidential election campaign, as seen from the suburbs.
articles.author: Sharon GAFFNEY

articles.title: Macron vows to replant Fontainebleau forest after devastating wildfires
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron on Thursday vowed to replant Fontainebleau forest after devastating wildfires blazed through at least 10% of the 20,000 hectare demain and forced hundreds of residents to flee. The historic forest, just south of Paris, draws hikers, climbers and nature lovers from all over the world every year.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: 'Tefal campaign': with Covid-19 monopolising voters' minds, nothing sticks
articles.summary: Presidential campaigns offer an abundance of catch phrases, whether slogans finessed by a candidate's team to deliver maximum impact or coined spontaneously on the trail. The proclamations – and gaffes – of presidential hopefuls bring texture to an election race and come to define a campaign, whether for a news cycle or forever in the history books. FRANCE 24 brings you the buzzwords of the 2022 French presidential race. In the spotlight: "Tefal campaign".
articles.author: Tracy MCNICOLL

articles.title: France records 300 excess deaths during unseasonal May heatwave
articles.summary: A five-day heatwave in May caused at least 300 more deaths than expected across France, health officials said Tuesday. The unseasonal heatwave was followed in June by 11 days of the hottest temperatures the country has experienced since records began.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: ‘Like working in a kettle’: France’s overcrowded prisons swelter under historic heatwave
articles.summary: The deadly heatwave sweeping France has once again exposed the structural problems of the country’s chronically overcrowded prisons, with groups of three or four detainees crammed into airless cells built to hold a lone prisoner. Analysts and prison staff alike have criticised a penal system that continues to see mass incarceration as the main means of cracking down on crime.
articles.author: Paul MILLAR

articles.title: Battle for the French far right: Zemmour, Le Pen try to steal each other's thunder
articles.summary: As France's April presidential election approaches, the campaign is getting under way in earnest. In this edition of our new show, we focus on the French Communist Party attempting a political comeback and discuss at length the battle raging between Eric Zemmour and Marine Le Pen for leadership of the French far right.
articles.author: Marc PERELMAN

articles.title: France ponders failure to protect children as school abuse scandal rocks Paris
articles.summary: Paris Mayor Emmanuel Grégoire has acknowledged “systemic” failings as investigators probe allegations of child abuse by non-teaching staff at more than 100 nurseries and primary schools in the French capital. The scandal has shocked the public and exposed major shortfalls in child protection and accountability.
articles.author: Benjamin DODMAN

articles.title: Former model accuses French scout of grooming her for Epstein
articles.summary: Former French model Juliette G said Daniel Siad, a French modelling scout with close ties to late sex offender Jeffrey Epstein, had groomer her with the aim of introducing her to potential abusers. Juliette, who has asked to withhold her surname to protect her privacy, is one of two ex-models to have accused Siad of grooming.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Libya ‘corruption pact’: Sarkozy returns to court as his former right-hand man turns against him
articles.summary: Former French president Nicolas Sarkozy was back in court Wednesday to answer questions regarding documents written by Claude Guéant, his onetime right-hand man and former interior minister. Guéant’s statements – and Sarkozy’s denials – are the latest chapter in a public falling-out as Sarkozy appeals his conviction for illegally accepting Libyan funds for his 2007 presidential campaign.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: France's public holidays: The art of the long weekend
articles.summary: France has a reputation, among some, of being a vacation nation. Is this warranted? In this edition of Entre Nous, we dive into France's public holidays during the month of May. We discuss the country's infamous long weekends or "ponts", an ongoing political fight over the May 1 bank holiday and what researchers say is the ideal number of "jours fériés" or public holidays.
articles.author: Solange MOUGIN

articles.title: Abuse at French after-school programmes: Parents sound the alarm
articles.summary: In Paris, parents are now dropping their children off at school in a climate of anxiety. For several months, reports of physical and sexual abuse involving nursery school children have been mounting. These cases are said to have taken place during after-school care and lunch breaks, when the children are supervised by non-teaching staff. In 2026 alone, 78 youth workers were suspended in Paris, 31 of them on suspicion of sexual abuse. Warning: viewers may find this report disturbing.
articles.author: Noémie ROCHE

articles.title: The rooftops of Paris with the zinc craftsmen of the sky
articles.summary: Paris’s slate-grey zinc rooftops are a key part of the French capital’s visual identity. They have long inspired painters and filmmakers and only exist thanks to the expertise of the roofers who install and maintain the galvanised metal covering many of Paris’s buildings. Their expertise could soon be included in UNESCO's intangible heritage list, as the profession adapts to the challenges of global warming.
articles.author: Olivia SALAZAR WINSPEAR

articles.title: France's top health advisory body wants compulsory vaccinations for health workers
articles.summary: France's top health advisory body recommended on Friday that coronavirus vaccinations should be made compulsory without delay for all health workers and other professionals who come into contact with people vulnerable to COVID-19.
articles.author: NEWS WIRES

articles.title: French navy boards Russia-linked tanker in Mediterranean
articles.summary: The French navy has boarded and seized an oil tanker sailing in the Western ‌Mediterranean from the Russian port of Murmansk accused of belonging to what has been dubbed Moscow's "shadow fleet", vessels of opaque ownership suspected of dodging Western sanctions on the country's crude oil exports.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Covid-19: French nightclubs reopen for the vaccinated
articles.summary: Nightlife fans across France can again crowd into clubs from Friday, despite warnings over a looming surge in Covid cases due to the more contagious Delta variant which looks set to become the dominant strain in the country as soon as this weekend.
articles.author: NEWS WIRES

articles.title: Socialist leads Paris mayoral race but leftist rival threatens to split vote
articles.summary: Socialist candidate Emmanuel Grégoire surged ahead of former culture minister Rachida Dati in the first round of voting for Paris mayor on Sunday as the left bids to extend its 25 years at the helm. But in the capital as in other cities across France, a strong showing by Jean-Luc Mélenchon's France Unbowed (LFI) could complicate matters for the mainstream left.
articles.author: Benjamin DODMAN

articles.title: French far right eyes Marseille upset after strong showing in mayoral elections
articles.summary: Candidates for the far-right National Rally posted strong results in the first round of France’s municipal elections on Sunday, winning several races outright and polling neck-and-neck with the incumbent left in Marseille, in the last major test of the French public mood ahead of next year’s all-important presidential election.
articles.author: Benjamin DODMAN

articles.title: Turnout low in French mayoral elections seen as key test ahead of 2027 presidential race
articles.summary: French voters cast ballots in municipal elections marred by low turnout on Sunday, in the last major test of the public mood ahead of next year’s all-important presidential election. The run-up to the vote was largely overshadowed by the Iran war and its fallout, notably the impact on fuel prices.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: ‘To be free, we have to be feared,’ Macron says in keynote nuclear speech
articles.summary: France will increase its nuclear warheads for the first time in decades, French President Emmanuel Macron announced on Monday, saying that “to be free, we have to be feared”. Macron delivered the update on the country’s nuclear strategy in a keynote speech from the military base hosting the nation's ballistic missile submarines.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Spain struggles to contain wildfires: 60,000 evacuated around Madrid
articles.summary: Spain has evacuated tens of thousands of people from villages west of the capital Madrid where wildfires and extremely dry conditions have been worsened by heatwaves and strong winds.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: UNESCO adds Normandy's D-Day landing beaches to World Heritage List
articles.summary: The D-Day landing beaches in Normandy were added to UNESCO's World Heritage List Sunday. The 80-kilometre stretch of coastline in northwest France served as the site for Allied forces' landing in Europe in June 1944, marking a decisive moment in the war against Nazi Germany and its fascist allies in Europe.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: 'We see a longer fire season nearly everywhere': Insight on Europe's wildfires
articles.summary: Stefan Doerr, the director of the Centre for Wildfire Research at Swansea University, speaks to FRANCE 24 about some of the reasons why fire seasons across the world seem to be getting more and more severe.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Spain fires: 'Firefighters are hoping that more of those fires don't join up'
articles.summary: FRANCE 24's Madrid correspondent Sarah Morris reports on what authorities have called a "difficult night" for the firefighters struggling to tackle the spreading wildfires near Madrid and Toledo.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Manhunt continues after man drives vehicle into Berlin Pride event
articles.summary: FRANCE 24 correspondent Nick Holdsworth reports from Berlin after a vehicle was driven into a crowd during the city's Pride event, killing one person and wounding 16 more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Van rams into Berlin Pride crowd, killing one and injuring 16
articles.summary: A van ploughed into crowds at Berlin's annual LGBTQ+ Pride celebrations on Saturday, killing one person and injuring at least 16 others before crashing into a tree. Police and prosecutors on Sunday issued a wanted notice for a 21-year-old identified only as Abdul B, and warned members of the public to avoid direct contact with him.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Spain: Wildfires force 70,000 people to evacuate in Madrid region
articles.summary: Sarah Morris has more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Nearly 98,000 hectares burned in France, a 'historic record' says government
articles.summary: The threat posed by a wildfire raging in the southwestern French department of Gironde "remains very serious," the top regional official, Sophie Brocas, said Saturday."The threat remains very serious. We are still facing a grave situation," she said, adding however that the blaze has lost "some of its intensity thanks to lower temperatures and increased humidity."
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Kazakhstan's president urges Putin to ‘freeze’ war in Ukraine
articles.summary: Kazakhstan's president on Saturday urged Russian leader Vladimir Putin to end the war in Ukraine during talks in the Siberian city of Omsk. Hours earlier, Ukrainian drones struck an oil refinery in Siberia in one of Kyiv's deepest attacks inside Russia.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Wildfires in Spain: Record temparatures accelerate spread of blazes
articles.summary: Another 25,000 people were evacuated from villages near Madrid threatened by wildfires, bringing the total who have fled to 70,000, Spain's government delegate to Madrid said on Saturday. The latest evacuations took place in the Valle del Tietar area of Avila province west of the capital, as well as two villages in the Madrid region, the official, Francisco Martin, told journalists.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Ukraine: Kyiv protests continue after Zelensky fires defense minister
articles.summary: Protesters in ​Kyiv on Friday announced an open ended rally demanding that President Volodymyr Zelensky reappoint ousted defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov after a badly explained government reshuffle escalated into a political crisis.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Ukrainians back ousted defence minister as political crisis brews
articles.summary: Peter Zalmayev, Director of the Eurasia Democracy Initiative, is our guest.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Climatologist warms of heatwaves, wildfires and rising risks in Europe
articles.summary: Jean-Pascal Van Ypersele, Professor of Climatology and Environnemental Sciencs at UCLouvain, is our guest.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Wildfires force nearly 260,000 people to evacuate in France and Spain
articles.summary: Massive wildfires sweeping southwestern France and central Spain forced nearly 260,000 people to flee on Saturday, as authorities deployed troops and additional firefighting aircraft to battle blazes fueled by extreme heat and drought.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: 'It smells of burning': Thousands evacuated as wildfires rage around Madrid
articles.summary: FRANCE 24's Madrid correspondent Sarah Morris shares the latest updates about firefighters' efforts to contain historic wildfires raging near the Spanish capital.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Macron says France will ‘rebuild' parts of country ravaged by wildfires
articles.summary: President Emmanuel Macron said Saturday that France would rebuild after wildfires ravaged parts of the country's south. "We will rebuild, we will repair and we will be there for as long as is needed," he said in a post on X. Read our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: ICC dismisses chief prosecutor Karim Khan over sexual misconduct allegations
articles.summary: Member states of the International Criminal Court (ICC) on Friday voted to dismiss chief prosecutor Karim Khan following allegations of sexual ⁠misconduct.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: #Ukraine targets Russian #ecommerce giant's warehouses in fourth #attack
articles.summary: #Ukraine struck several warehouses owned by the so-called '#Russian #Amazon' #Wildberries on July 24, which it says supplies the Russian army. A separate attack on a factory killed at least six people, while Russian strikes just outside #Kyiv killed at least ten.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Giorgia Meloni's Italy: An authoritarian drift? (Part 2)
articles.summary: In this edition of Europe Rendezvous, we travel to Italy, one of the European Union's founding members, to examine how the country's democratic institutions have come under increasing pressure. It may be the season of la dolce vita, but life has been far from sweet for migrants, women seeking abortions in parts of Italy, and journalists facing growing political pressure on the media. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni leads a coalition of conservatives and the far right, and as the 2027 elections approach, her government has been accused of seeking greater influence over the judiciary, the media and the electoral system.
articles.author: Armen GEORGIAN

articles.title: Giorgia Meloni's Italy: An authoritarian drift? (Part 1)
articles.summary: In this edition of Europe Rendezvous, we travel to Italy, one of the European Union's founding members, to examine how the country's democratic institutions have come under increasing pressure. It may be the season of la dolce vita, but life has been far from sweet for migrants, women seeking abortions in parts of Italy, and journalists facing growing political pressure on the media. Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni leads a coalition of conservatives and the far right, and as the 2027 elections approach, her government has been accused of seeking greater influence over the judiciary, the media and the electoral system.
articles.author: Armen GEORGIAN

articles.title: US holds fire against Iran as media reports say Washington's stockpiles are dwindling
articles.summary: Another night has passed without further US air strikes on Iran after nearly two weeks of nightly bombardments. US media reports that Washington's concerns over dwindling stockpiles of Patriot interceptors and other air defence munitions could be behind the pause in fighting.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: War in the Middle East: Deadly violence mounts in the West Bank
articles.summary: Nomi Bar-Yaacov, renowned international negotiator, arbitrator and mediator, is our guest.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: UNESCO adds West Bank site, Lebanese castles to World Heritage List despite Israeli opposition
articles.summary: UNESCO added a major archaeological site in the West Bank and a group of historic castles in southern Lebanon to its World Heritage List, defying Israeli objections and reigniting a long-running dispute over the intersection of cultural heritage and politics in the region.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: No, this video does not show Iran downing a US B-52 bomber
articles.summary: A video said to show an Iranian missile destroying a US B-52 bomber has garnered more than three million views on X, where it has been picked up and shared by a pro-Iranian account. However, if you look closely, you’ll see the signs that this video was actually artificially generated.
articles.author: The FRANCE 24 Observers

articles.title: Palestinians bury four people killed in occupied West Bank clash with Israeli settlers
articles.summary: Grieving family members on Saturday buried four Palestinian men killed during a clash with Israeli settlers a day earlier in the occupied West Bank. Palestinians reported a series of violent settler attacks on other villages in the Palestinian territory late Friday following the deadly confrontation, with local officials saying Israelis had set fire to olive groves in Farata and opened fire on people trying to extinguish the blaze.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Middle East: Red Sea tensions grow as Saudi-Houthi clashes open new front
articles.summary: The Houthis have accused US ally Riyadh of a "dangerous escalation" after it struck military targets belonging to the group on Friday, following the rebels announcing a maritime blockade of the top oil producer and hitting its ships in the Red Sea.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: UNESCO adds Sebastia site to World Heritage List despite Israeli objections
articles.summary: A United Nations committee on Friday inscribed a major archaeological site in the West Bank and a group of castles in southern Lebanon on the World Heritage List, despite objections from Israel, which had urged the committee to reject the bids. The decision at a U.N. Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization meeting in South Korea came days after Israel’s Foreign Ministry urged the committee to reject efforts to designate the small West Bank town of Sebastia and the Lebanese castles, calling the nominations a “weaponization of cultural heritage.”
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Guterres arrives in Syria for first UN secretary-general visit since before civil war
articles.summary: UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres touched down in Damascus Saturday for a three-day visit where he is expected to reaffirm support for the multi-confessional country's efforts to rebuild after more than a decade of bloody civil war.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Houthis target Saudi oil facilities as fighting on new Middle East front intensifies
articles.summary: Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels launched missiles and drones at Saudi Arabia's oil infrastructure on Saturday, retaliating for Saudi strikes in Yemen and intensifying a regional conflict that is increasingly threatening energy supplies and vital shipping lanes.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: US pummels Iran as Tehran targets regional bases stationing US forces
articles.summary: Iran on Friday said it carried out attacks targeting US military assets and bases with US forces in Bahrain, Jordan and Kuwait in retaliation for Washington's latest strikes across the country. The US meanwhile bombarded sites across Iran as the conflict escalated, leading US embassies to alert its nationals across the region.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Arrests, denials and missing images: Gulf states’ response to Iranian strikes
articles.summary: Since the conflict between Iran and the United States began on February 28, more than 1,000 people have been arrested for attempting to document Iranian strikes in Jordan and Gulf countries allied with Washington. The governments of these countries have sought to deter the circulation of such images and maintain an official narrative denying that the strikes reached their targets.
articles.author: The FRANCE 24 Observers

articles.title: Deadly clashes in the occupied West Bank
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has vowed to respond with "full force" following a deadly clash in the occupied West Bank. Two Israeli soldiers were killed on Friday in fighting near the settlement of Havat Gilad and the neighbouring village of Tal. The incident comes amid a sharp rise in violence across the West Bank since the start of the Gaza war in October 2023.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Iran warns countries aiding US attack
articles.summary: Middle East tensions are once again driving up global oil prices, with Brent crude climbing above $100 a barrel for the first time since May. While much of the focus has been on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, the alternative shipping route through the Red Sea is becoming increasingly dangerous after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they targeted two Saudi oil tankers. The escalation comes as US President Donald Trump said on Thursday he was considering a "massive attack" on Iran, prompting Tehran to warn it would hold accountable any country that assists the United States in such an operation. France 24 International Affairs Editor Andrew Hilliar shares further insights.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: 'Incredibly dire': Nine months into Gaza ceasefire, conditions 'should have improved by now'
articles.summary: Alison Sargent is pleased to welcome Shaina Low, Communications Advisor for the Norwegian Refugee Council's Palestine mission. Despite the reduction in large scale hostilities Low argues that Gaza remains trapped in a state of structural emergency, where humanitarian actors are prevented from moving beyond short term relief because of extensive restrictions on aid, construction materials, fuel, and operational access. She asserts that the central issue is no longer simply the scale of destruction, but the inability to reverse it despite the existence of a ceasefire.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Gaza faces ongoing food crisis despite ceasefire
articles.summary: More than nine months into the ceasefire between Israel and Hamas, two-thirds of Gaza's population is still facing crisis levels of food insecurity, according to a new UN report released on Thursday. The report warns that recent gains could quickly be reversed unless humanitarian agencies continue to receive sustained access to the enclave, along with adequate funding and stability. For more on the humanitarian situation, we're joined by Shana Low, Communications Adviser for the Norwegian Refugee Council's Palestine mission, speaking to us from Amman, Jordan.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Oil prices surge above $100 a barrel for first time since May
articles.summary: Global oil prices have surged once again as tensions in the Middle East continue to escalate. Brent crude has climbed above $100 a barrel for the first time since May. While much of the focus has been on the strategic Strait of Hormuz, shipping through the Red Sea is also coming under growing threat after Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels said they targeted two Saudi oil tankers. The escalation comes as Donald Trump said he was considering a "massive attack" on Iran, prompting Tehran to warn it would hold accountable any country supporting a US strike. Peter O'Brien reports.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Netanyahu orders new West Bank settler outposts, legalises existing ones after deadly clash
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Friday said his government would establish new settler outposts in the occupied West Bank and legalise more existing ones, after a deadly clash left two Israeli and four Palestinians dead.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Trump says US and Iran are talking, but Tehran not yet ready for a deal
articles.summary: President Donald ​Trump on Friday said the US and Iran were ​in ‌talks to negotiate ⁠an end to their ‌conflict, but repeated that ⁠Tehran was not yet ready for a ​deal. In Yemen, the Houthis said they were not seeking to close the key Bab al-Mandeb Strait and that their naval blockade in the Red Sea was solely aimed at Saudi Arabia. Read about the day’s events as they unfolded on our liveblog.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Trump threatens Iran and Houthi rebels with 'major military punishment'
articles.summary: Iran and the United States threatened to intensify attacks on Thursday after Yemen's Houthi rebels struck Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, driving Brent crude above $100 a barrel and fuelling fears of a widening regional conflict and renewed pressure on the global economy.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Trump stuns Saudis by pinning nuclear deal to Israel ties
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump said Thursday that a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia depends on the kingdom recognizing Israel -- throwing the agreement into turmoil just the day after it was signed. Riyadh has long resisted joining the so-called Abraham Accords with Israel, insisting especially after the Gaza conflict on a pathway to a Palestinian state. FRANCE 24's Emerald Maxwell reports.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Why Iran is targeting Kuwait's desalination plants as part of its war strategy
articles.summary: Iranian strikes targeted Kuwait’s desalination and power plants for the fourth consecutive day on Monday. The attacks are putting unprecedented pressure on a Gulf country heavily dependant on desalination for its water supply. Iran is attempting to wage a “psychological war” on a country with few options for striking back, according to some analysts.
articles.author: Sophian AUBIN

articles.title: Trump says Saudi nuclear deal contingent on Riyadh normalising relations with Israel
articles.summary: President Donald Trump on Thursday set a new condition to a US-Saudi nuclear deal signed the previous day by insisting the agreement was "totally subject to" the Gulf kingdom joining the Abraham Accords. Riyadh has resisted normalising relations with Israel, especially after the Gaza war, and the new condition throws the US-Saudi deal into turmoil.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Middle East war's economic impact 'could get worse' if Houthis join in
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump threatened Yemen's Houthi rebels with "major military punishment" after they launched missile and drone strikes on oil tankers in the Red Sea. Concern has sparked across the globe regarding the rebels' involvement in the war. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: US rhetoric 'all about amping up' but strategy for a deal with Iran unclear
articles.summary: After a twelfth night of US strikes, Iran has hit US bases in Jordan and Kuwait, claiming several military assets were destroyed. This also comes after rebel Houthis in Yemen struck two Saudi oil tankers in the Red Sea, further expanding the conflict. FRANCE 24's Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: How Houthi strikes on oil tankers will impact the Middle East war
articles.summary: Yemen's Houthi rebels say they have attacked two Saudi oil tankers. The Houthis are supported by Iran, and the attacks in the Red Sea could be a new front for the war between the US and Iran. But how will this affect the conflict?
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: US and Saudi Arabia reach a multi-billion dollar civilian nuclear deal
articles.summary: The United States announced that it had reached a civilian nuclear cooperation deal with Saudi Arabia. Energy Secretary Chris Wright signed the pact and a separate bilateral safeguards deal alongside Saudi Energy Minister Prince Abdulaziz bin Salman. There have been years of discussions even under the Biden administration as part of a larger deal where Saudi Arabia would normalise relations with Israel. That fell apart after the October 7th attacks. There's likely to be pushback from allies and those concerned with safety.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Replay: Marco Rubio addresses Middle East and Ukraine conflicts
articles.summary: Rewatch as US Secretary of State Marco Rubio addresses the conflicts in the Middle East and Ukraine at the end of the ASEAN summit in Manilla.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: UN chief says Middle East conflict is at the 'edge of the imaginable'
articles.summary: Ongoing conflict in the Middle East has pushed the region to the "edge of the unimaginable", UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres warned on Thursday, as Houthi attacks on shipping in the Red Sea threatened to escalate the conflict further. President Donald Trump said the US would hold Iran responsible for these attacks, as the rebels threatened a naval blockade. Follow our liveblog to see how the day's events unfolded.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: ICC asked to look into xenophobic violence in South Africa
articles.summary: In tonight's show, Ghanaian nationals submit request to the ICC calling for an investigation into months of Xenophobic violence against migrants in South Africa. Also, around 20 people die in AFD attack in Eastern DRC as the Islamic state affiliated group steps up attacks. And Coconut trees, once a common site on Ivory coasts coastlines, are slowly disappearing under renewed waves of deforestation and rapid urbanisation; and it threatens an entire sector and local ecosystem.
articles.author: Clémence WALLER

articles.title: Ghana activists call for laws to protect people accused of witchcraft
articles.summary: In tonight's edition, North Africa is in the grip of a severe heatwave, with temperatures nearing 49 degrees Celsius. Also, six years after the brutal killing of a 90-year-old woman accused of witchcraft shocked Ghana and the world, activists say the fight for justice remains far from over. And, the Kigali Cine Junction is bringing five days of screenings, workshops and industry discussions to audiences across Rwanda.
articles.author: Clarisse FORTUNÉ

articles.title: Ghana’s president asks for AU debate on South Africa’s ‘escalating xenophobic attacks’
articles.summary: Ghanaian President John Mahama on Thursday called for an African Union (AU) debate to "formally address the escalating xenophobic attacks" on foreign nationals in South Africa. More than 160,000 foreign nationals have left South Africa and several have died over the past two months amid rising hostility against undocumented migrants.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: DR Congo's Ebola outbreak becomes fastest ever recorded
articles.summary: The number of deaths in the current Ebola epidemic in the DRC has now topped 1,000, and the number of confirmed cases is around 2500. Experts are calling for more funding to help tackle the crisis as it becomes the fastest spreading outbreak ever recorded.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Crucial salt trade revives as Pink Lake slowly recovers from floods
articles.summary: Salt harvesters in Senegal are once again seeing the world through rose tinted glasses. The famous Pink Lake is slowly finding its rosy colours four years after flooding almost destroyed its delicate ecosystem and the economy built around it.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Systemic use of 'goons' in Kenya amplifies political repression
articles.summary: With one year to go before Kenya's 2027 presidential election, human rights organizations are sounding the alarm. They are denouncing the rise of “goons”—henchmen recruited by political leaders to infiltrate rallies, sow chaos, and intimidate opponents. This is a long-standing phenomenon that has worsened significantly since the large-scale protests against William Ruto’s government.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Ebola outbreak kills over 1,000 people in DR Congo
articles.summary: In tonight's edition, the Ebola outbreak in the DRC has crossed a devastating threshold, with more than 1,000 lives lost. Also, in Kenya, human rights groups warn that political “goons” are increasingly being used to disrupt rallies ahead of elections next year. And, in Senegal, four years after devastating floods threatened the famous Pink Lake’s unique ecosystem, the lake is slowly regaining its iconic colour.
articles.author: Clarisse FORTUNÉ

articles.title: Senegal's Bassirou Diomaye Faye backs Macky Sall for UN top job
articles.summary: Senegal will support Macky Sall’s candidacy for the post of Secretary-General of the United Nations. The announcement was made in a press release on Monday, three days after he was granted an audience with current President Bassirou Diomaye Faye. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Dakar, Aminatou Diallo.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Two foreign jihadists arrested in Nigeria for helping local terror groups
articles.summary: After 17 years, the Nigeria military’s efforts to contend a jihadist insurgency do not seem to be successful. The military is facing fresh hurdles with foreign fighters, including those from the Middle East joining the insurgents. The foreigners are bringing skills and technology that have proved very valuable in the Jihadists’ fight against the military. Details by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Lagos, Sam Olukoya.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Mounting violence in Mali poses threat to military-led government
articles.summary: Mali’s military has suffered one of its deadliest losses in years. At least 50 soldiers were killed in an ambush near the northern town of Anefis, in an attack claimed by Tuareg separatists and Al-Qaeda-linked jihadists. The assault is the latest in a string of setbacks, with militants also targeting Malian and Russian Africa Corps forces, downing a military helicopter, and briefly seizing territory. More with Hénio Nsaibia, West Africa Senior Analyst at ACLED.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Senegal makes U-turn to back ex-president Sall for UN chief
articles.summary: In tonight's edition, a deadly ambush in northern Mali leaves at least 50 soldiers dead. Also, Nigeria is facing a new challenge in its fight against jihadist insurgents as foreign fighters join armed groups. And Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye is backing former president Macky Sall's bid to become UN Secretary-General.
articles.author: Clarisse FORTUNÉ

articles.title: UN says 144 migrants and refugees reported dead or missing off the coast of Mauritania
articles.summary: The UN refugee agency said Tuesday that 144 people were reported dead or missing following "tragic maritime incidents" off the coast of Mauritania last week. Two children who were brought safely ashore from one of the sinking boats had lost all of their families during the journey from Gambia.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: DRC president agrees to open national dialogue amid mounting political pressure
articles.summary: In the Democratic Republic of Congo, President Felix Tshisekedi has agreed to open national talks with the political opposition. The move comes as the Tshisekedi administration experiences intensified political pressure over its proposal to amend the constitution. The agreement to engage in an open dialogue marks a significant political step in a country where civil society groups have been calling for a national dialogue for over a year.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: What to know about the West African economic summit seeking regional reform
articles.summary: The 69th ECOWAS summit was held on July 19th in Freetown, Sierra Leone.The outgoing Chair of the ECOWAS Conference of Heads of State and Government, Julius Maada Bio, set the tone by calling for “far-reaching changes” within the West African economic organisation.The meeting was also marked by the Senegalese Head of State taking up the rotating presidency of ECOWAS, as well as by strong criticism from Guinea, which condemned the sanctions imposed by the organisation in recent years.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Morocco's Tangier hosts first edition of its photography festival
articles.summary: Tangier, Morocco's iconic port city and gateway between Europe and North Africa, is hosting the first edition of the International photography festival "Photo Tangier". This year's theme is "The Call of the Open Sea". The event will span two and a half months, from the 17th June to the 31st August, transforming Tangier into an open air creative space in which private galleries, museums, and public spaces come together as one big work of art.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: 'We're living in fear': 19 million children in Nigeria are out of school to avoid kidnappings
articles.summary: The 46 children and teachers that were abducted on May 15th in southwestern state of Oyo were rescued and reunited with their families on July 10th. Since the dramatic abduction of the Chibok schoolgirls in 2014, Nigeria has been hit with waves of mass kidnappings from schools. 27% of children in Nigeria are out of school, one of the highest rates in the world. The threat of abduction serves as one of the biggest obstacles to children pursuing their education.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Senegalese president becomes chairman of West African economic union
articles.summary: In tonight's edition: Senegalese President Bassirou Diomaye Faye takes the helm of the Economic Community of West African States (ECOWAS). Also, nearly 19 million Nigerian children are out of school, as the threat of kidnapping is keeping many classrooms empty. Also, Tangier is celebrating the art of visual storytelling with the International Photography Festival.
articles.author: Clarisse FORTUNÉ

articles.title: Spain PM Sanchez visits Algeria for first time in four years as ties thaw
articles.summary: Spain’s Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez on Monday visited Algeria for the first time in four years in a bid to mend diplomatic ties between the two countries after they were frayed by a row over Western Sahara. In 2022, Madrid abandoned its neutrality stance over the disputed territory and backed Morocco’s sovereignty claim, angering Algiers. The thaw began last year, when Algeria reactivated a friendship treaty it had suspended over the dispute.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Senegal changes course to back ex-leader Macky Sall as UN chief
articles.summary: The Senegalese government on Monday made a U-turn, announcing it would back former president Macky Sall’s candidacy to replace UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres when his term expires. The government had previously declined to throw its weight behind Sall, whom it accuses of deadly political repression while in office, but reversed course after he paid the sitting president a visit in Dakar this weekend.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: At least 50 Malian soldiers killed in rebel-jihadist attack
articles.summary: At least 50 Malian soldiers were killed and dozens more were taken prisoner in an attack by Tuareg separatists and jihadists, local sources told AFP on Sunday.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Malian army convoy ambushed by rebels north of Gao
articles.summary: A Malian army convoy was ambushed by rebels in a remote part of the northern Gao region, the Malian military confirmed Saturday. Regional al Qaeda affiliate JNIM and the separatist Azawad Liberation Front (FLA) claimed responsibility for the attack in separate statements that cited "great human losses".
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Ethiopian Drill explodes on the streets of Addis Ababa
articles.summary: Last year, the aggressive genre of Drill could only be heard on social media in Ethiopia. But over the last few months the fast-paced, often matched with violent lyrics, style of hip hop has exploded on the streets of Addis Ababa, taking over mainstream bars and nightclubs. For some, its rapid popularity is due to Gen Z's lack of political and economic certainty. But Ethiopia remains a very conservative country, and not everyone is a fan of Drill. This report by our correspondent Tom Canetti.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Ethiopia: New refugee support centre opens in Addis Ababa
articles.summary: The UN refugee agency and the Ethiopian government have opened a new support centre in Addis Ababa to provide refugees with free legal advice and access to essential services. The initiative aims to help refugees navigate bureaucracy, obtain vital documents and improve their chances of finding work. Ethiopia hosts more than one million refugees, making it Africa's third-largest refugee-hosting country. Tom Canetti reports from Addis Ababa.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Project 'Afrika’: Inside Russia's propaganda machine
articles.summary: After a leak of confidential documents revealed how Russian agents have been placing hundreds of articles in French-speaking media outlets in West and Central Africa, FRANCE 24 travelled to Dakar, Senegal, to investigate this secret operation.
articles.author: The FRANCE 24 Observers

articles.title: Who are Russia's 3,000 African army recruits fighting in Ukraine?
articles.summary: Russia continues to recruit Africans to fight on the front in Ukraine. The Stop Russian Recruiters platform, which is linked to Urkaine's Ministry of Defence, has now identified nearly 3,000 recruits. Around one in six has already been killed. Among the countries most affected are Cameroon, Ghana, Egypt and Kenya, where FRANCE 24's Bastien Renouil tells us more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: 'Project Afrika': Inside Russia's propaganda machine
articles.summary: This week in Reporters: a special report by FRANCE 24's The Observers. After a leak of confidential documents revealed how Russian agents have been planting hundreds of articles in French-speaking media outlets in West and Central Africa, FRANCE 24 travelled to Dakar, Senegal, to investigate this secret operation. Nathan Gallo and Derek Thomson report, with footage by Aminatou Diallo.
articles.author: Nathan GALLO

articles.title: Ebola 'spreading faster than any previous outbreak' in DR Congo, WHO warns
articles.summary: The World Health Organization on Thursday warned that the Ebola virus is spreading through the Democratic Republic of Congo faster than during any previous outbreak, with more than 2,000 confirmed cases and 796 deaths recorded in just two months. Health officials say the rapid spread, lack of approved vaccine for the virus strain and ongoing conflict in the country are complicating efforts to contain the epidemic.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: DR Congo's healthcare workers go on strike as Ebola epidemic spreads
articles.summary: Health workers fighting the Ebola outbreak in DR Congo are going on strike over unpaid wages. This comes as the World Health Organization warned that Ebola was spreading in the Democratic Republic of Congo at a faster pace than during any previous outbreak of the deadly virus. More than 2,000 Ebola cases, including 754 deaths, have been recorded in DRC. FRANCE 24's Emmet Livingstone tells us more about the strikes.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Flavio Bolsonaro launches presidential bid in Brazil despite challenges
articles.summary: Flavio Bolsonaro on Saturday formally launched his campaign for Brazil's October presidential election, seeking to extend his family's grip on the country's far-right movement despite a series of scandals that have dented his once-strong challenge to incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Venezuela honors thousands of victims one month since earthquakes
articles.summary: Venezuelans across the quake zone and in the capital Caracas held a minute of silence Friday to honor victims of the tremors that struck one month ago.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Trump praises secret service at White House correspondents' dinner
articles.summary: Fraser Jackson has more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship splashes down in Indian Ocean after successful test flight
articles.summary: US aerospace company SpaceX carried out a successful test flight of its14-storey Starship rocket Friday, blasting off from Texas to land gently in the waters of the Indian Ocean. It's the first such success since US tech billionaire Elon Musk's SpaceX went public in June.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Trump lashes out at 'fake news' and jokes about 2028 presidential run in press gala do-over
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump delivered an at-times rambling speech at the rescheduled White House Correspondents' Dinner Friday, three months after an alleged assassination attempt brought the annual event to an abrupt halt. Trump notably joked about running for a third presidential term in 2028, which is barred under the US Constitution.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Trump to speak at rescheduled White House Correspondents’ Dinner following failed April shooting
articles.summary: Nearly three months after a botched shooting cut the annual White House press gala short, US President Donald Trump is expected to speak at a rescheduled dinner held at the Waldorf Astoria hotel Friday. The event will take place under heightened security.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Six candidates vying to become the next UN secretary after Guterres
articles.summary: Six candidates vying to become the next UN secretary-general presented their visions for the organisation on Thursday, as the United Nations faces a financial and confidence crisis ahead of a selection process that will determine its leadership from January 2027. France 24 International affairs editor Kethevane Gorjestani shares further insights on candidates.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: US hits partners with new tariffs over forcer labour claims
articles.summary: Starting this Friday, the United States will impose new tariffs on imports from 60 trading partners, covering 99 percent of all goods entering the country. The new measures replace the temporary 10 percent global tariff introduced 150 days ago after the Supreme Court struck down President Donald Trump's previous sweeping tariff plan. The administration says the latest tariffs are aimed at addressing concerns over goods produced with forced labour. Peter O'Brien reports.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: UN leadership candidates outline visions ahead of secretary-general race
articles.summary: Six candidates vying to become the next UN secretary-general presented their visions for the organisation on Thursday, as the United Nations faces a financial and confidence crisis ahead of a selection process that will determine its leadership from January 2027.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Fields medal honours four mathematicians as AI reshapes the profession
articles.summary: The International Mathematical Union awarded the prestigious Fields Medal to four mathematicians on Thursday, including only the third woman to receive the honour, as researchers weighed the growing impact of artificial intelligence on a field increasingly being reshaped by the technology.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Trump announces double digit tariffs on 60 countries over forced labour concerns
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump imposed new tariffs of up to 12.5% on imports from 60 countries on Thursday, replacing temporary levies that expire on Friday after the Supreme Court struck down his earlier trade measures. The White House said the duties target countries that have failed to curb imports made with forced labour.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Virginia Governor Abigail Spanberger: 'No single blueprint for the Democratic Party'
articles.summary: A rising star among Democratic Party moderates, Virginia’s first woman governor, Abigail Spanberger, was elected on the same night last November as New York City mayor Zohran Mamdani, a Democratic socialist. In a wide-ranging interview with François Picard, Spanberger outlines a pragmatic vision of politics rooted in coalition-building, institutional trust and addressing voters’ everyday concerns through practical governance rather than ideological confrontation.
articles.author: François PICARD

articles.title: Sex trafficking in fashion: 'Outrageous that French legal system hasn't done anything by now'
articles.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Dana Thomas, Paris-based journalist, specialising in fashion and culture, and author of "Deluxe: How Luxury Lost Its Luster". For decades, allegations of sexual exploitation in the fashion industry, spanning the globe, have resurfaced, often surrounding powerful figures whose deaths have complicated any semblance of accountability. In the wake of Daniel Siad's sudden death, Thomas offers a scathing indictment of the systemic failures within French law enforcement, the modelling industry, and the highest echelons of power.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: #Gaza: #Mamdani urges government to arrest #Netanyahu if he visits #US
articles.summary: In a video posted to social media on July 21, #NYC mayor Zohran #Mamdani urges the US federal government to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin #Netanyahu if he visits the #US later this year, after admitting he does not have the authority to enforce the #ICC's arrest warrant.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Trump to announce US-Saudi nuclear deal to allow fuel enrichment
articles.summary: The New York Times is reporting that the Trump administration plans to announce that it has reached a broad nuclear agreement with Saudi Arabia which could lead to the country enriching its own fuel for nuclear reactors.What do we know about the deal and what will this mean for the region? Details by Angela Diffley, FRANCE 24 international affairs editor.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Trump to announce landmark nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia
articles.summary: According to US media, the Trump administration is expected to announce a nuclear deal with Saudi Arabia later this Wednesday. While the White House claims the nuclear deal will bring billions to American companies and pave the way for Saudis to have a civilian nuclear program and nuclear power, critics of the yet announced deal fear that it could open the door for the kingdom to attain a nuclear weapon. Solange Mougin explains what we know so far.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Mamdani says New York City can't arrest Netanyahu for war crimes but federal government should
articles.summary: New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani said Tuesday that his administration did not have the legal authority to arrest Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as he had planned, and called on US federal authorities to do so. The Democratic mayor had said earlier this month that he was exploring the legal possibility of executing the arrest warrant issued by the International Criminal Court against the Israeli leader if he were to attend the UN General Assembly in September.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Trump announces 100% tariffs on imported generic pharmaceutical drugs
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump announced a 100% tariff on imported generic pharmaceutical drugs on Tuesday. The tariff, which aims to bolster US pharmaceutical production, is set to go into effect in August 2028.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Canada evaluating 'all options' after fresh US tariffs threat
articles.summary: Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney said Tuesday he was looking at "all options" after US President Donald Trump made plans to impose new 50 percent tariffs on many Canadian goods in 30 days. Carney also said that he and Trump had agreed to "intensify discussions" in the coming weeks on a possible deal, but did not suggest he would travel to Washington for any talks. FRANCE 24's Christopher Guly reports from Ottawa.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Joseph Aoun in Washington: Bilal Saab firmly believes 'this meeting couldn't have gone any better'
articles.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Bilal Saab, Senior Managing Director of the Trends Research Group and a close friend of Lebanese President Joseph Aoun. Mr. Saab offers a cautiously optimistic assessment of a pivotal moment in Lebanese diplomacy, arguing that President Aoun's visit to Washington represents an important opportunity to consolidate international backing for Lebanon's sovereignty and state institutions. While acknowledging the formidable structural challenges posed by Hezbollah, regional tensions, and extremely complex Israeli-Lebanese security challenges, Mr. Saab contends that success will not come from military coercion, but rather a focus on the gradual strengthening of the Lebanese state. According to Mr. Saab, Lebanon is both a testing ground for American regional diplomacy and a fragile experiment in state-building that will require sustained political support and not symbolic declarations.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: 'Mostly symbolic': Does Aoun's White House visit signal a 'new containment strategy towards Iran'?
articles.summary: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Nadim Houry, Executive Director of the Arab Reform Initiative. He offers a nuanced assessment of Lebanon's diplomatic and long-term strategic challenges, arguing that President Joseph Aoun's visit to Washington is less about immediate policy breakthroughs than about repositioning Lebanon within an evolving regional order. Houry highlights the interconnected nature of Lebanese politics, Israeli security calculations, U.S. regional strategy, Iranian influence, and Hezbollah's evolving role, suggesting that none of these issues can be understood in isolation.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Guyana ferry capsizes, leaving dozens dead and scores missing
articles.summary: At least 27 people died after a ferry capsized off Guyana, Prime Minister Mark Phillips said Monday, as rescuers searched for 83 people still missing. Sixty-nine passengers have been rescued since the MV Barima overturned Saturday night while traveling from Georgetown to the inland Essequibo region, Phillips said.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: North America's 2026 FIFA World Cup: From Spain's fierce tactical victory to Messi's enduring legacy
articles.summary: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Robbie Knock, Lead Commentator and sports journalist. The 2026 FIFA World Cup will be remembered not only for Spain's triumph on the pitch but also for the way football became enmeshed in politics, entertainment, institutional scrutiny, and the closing chapter of one of the sport's greatest careers. Robbie Knock argues that Spain's victory was the product of tactical superiority rather than fortune, while acknowledging that controversial refereeing decisions complicated perceptions of the tournament. He also presents Lionel Messi's expected international farewell as the conclusion of a defining era in world football, emphasising that dignity in defeat may ultimately reinforce rather than diminish his legacy.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: At least six dead after earthquake hits Peru's Andes
articles.summary: In the Andes, a 5.5 magnitude earthquake has hit Peru. At least six people died in the quake and more than 30 have been injured, according to local authorities. Damage was compounded by the area's rustic constructions - adding to that that the earthquake's epicenter was close to the surface.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Cuban dissident artist arrives in US after 5-years in prison
articles.summary: A hero's welcome for Luis Manuel Otero Alcántara as he arrived in Miami following his release from prison in Cuba. The dissident artist accepted exile after the United States granted him humanitarian parole. Otero Alcántara co-founded the San Isidro Movement, a collective of Havana-based artists, writers, and musicians that protests against the Cuban government. In 2021, he was arrested in Havana during anti-government demonstrations and was later sentenced to five years in prison on charges of public disorder, contempt, and disrespect for national symbols. Carla Colomé Santiago, a Cuban journalist based in Miami, shares her insights.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: The week in pictures: The end of the World Cup, heatwaves and wildfires, war in Ukraine
articles.summary: The final stages of the World Cup, with Les Bleus’ elimination and England finishing third; extreme heat and wildfires around the world; and the Tour de France brought to a standstill by the heatwave in France. FRANCE 24 looks back at some of the week's most striking images.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: World Cup final: Argentina face Spain
articles.summary: Argentina face Spain in a highly anticipated clash between Lionel Messi and teenage sensation Lamine Yamal. With football's biggest prize at stake, Selina Sykes looks ahead to the showdown.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India's 'cockroach' party says ending protest after minister resigns
articles.summary: Andrew Hilliar analyses the situation.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India’s 'Cockroach' movement ends protests after education minister resigns
articles.summary: Sarah Jacob has more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India's education minister resigns in major victory for youth protesters
articles.summary: Navodita Kumari has more.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Indian education minister resigns after mass protests over exam paper leaks
articles.summary: India's Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan said on Saturday he had resigned from his post following mass protests calling for his dismissal. Public trust in India's university testing system has been undermined by a series of exam irregularities, including the leaking of a medical entrance question paper that forced more than two million candidates to re-sit the test.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Protests grow as Cockroach Janta Party says talks with government stall
articles.summary: #Protests are still growing in #India. The #Cockroach Janta Party says there was no breakthrough during a second round of talks with the #government. Demonstrators are still demanding the education minister Dharmendra #Pradhan resign following an exam paper leak, but other issues are coming to light as one of the protesters told FRANCE 24.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Why are India's youth protesting?
articles.summary: The Cockroach Janta Party began as a satirical youth movement just a few months ago, but has since emerged as a rallying point for disillusioned young people across India. So, what's driving the growing frustration and wave of protests? Rachael Griffiths explains.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India youth movement agrees to talk but insists protests will continue
articles.summary: India has extended a mobile internet shutdown in the capital, New Delhi, as Prime Minister Narendra Modi faces his biggest youth-led challenge since taking office in 2014. Leaders of the youth-led "Cockroach" movement are due to meet government officials later today in an effort to resolve a standoff over the country's education system. The talks come hours after activist Sonam Wangchuk ended a 26-day hunger strike, amid growing public anger over a series of exam irregularities and other scandals. France 24 correspondent Sarah Jacob reports from New Delhi.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Indian activist ends 26-day hunger strike, though student protests continue
articles.summary: Indian activist Sonam Wangchuk ended his 26-day hunger strike on Friday after talks with government ministers, but student-led protests over leaked medical entrance exam papers continued, with demonstrators demanding the education minister's resignation and wider reforms.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Indian youth 'not scared anymore': Modi and BJP party's 'architecture of fear has met its match'
articles.summary: Angela Diffley is pleased to welcome Anish Gawande, National Spokesperson for the Nationalist Congress Party (NCP). According to Mr. Gawande, India's student protests represent a generational rupture in Indian politics: the emergence of a politically fearless youth challenging a decade-long "architecture of fear" under Narendra Modi's government. He contends that the movement is about accountability rather than education policy, exposing a widening gap between a government accustomed to political dominance and a generation unwilling to accept opacity or state intimidation.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: How the student 'Cockroach' movement grew its influence across India
articles.summary: Young Indians are keeping up the pressure - continuing their demands for the Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan - to step down. This as their online satirical group the "Cockroach People's Party" grows in stature and support. It won millions of followers on social media and tens of thousands of sign-ups since its launch in May.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India's 'Cockroach' movement spreads to Mumbai after violence in New Delhi
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has finally broken his silence on the student protest movement known as the “Cockroach Janta Party”. The protests have spread from the capital New Delhi to other large cities including Mumbai and Bengaluru. Clashes with the police have occurred in several cities as well.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India's police accused of exercising 'absolute brutality' against peaceful protesters
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has vowed "stringent punishment" for those involved in exam fraud that fuelled student anger. Those are his first direct comments tied to the major protests challenging his government. Meanwhile, the movement has spread from the capital city to other major cities. FRANCE 24's Sarah Jacob tells us about the latest.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Modi vows punishment for exam fraud as 'Cockroach' protests spread
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi has finally broken his silence on the student protest movement known as the Cockroach Janta Party. He said that his government will move to swiftly punish those responsible for the leak of answers that forced the cancellation of the country's undergrad medical exam for some 2.2 million students. That scandal sparked a youth-led revolt determined to force the ouster of the country's education minister. The protests have spread from the capital New Delhi to other large cities including Mumbai and Bengaluru.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Modi vows 'stringent punishment' for exam fraud fuelling India's youth-led 'Cockroach' protests
articles.summary: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi on Thursday vowed to punish those involved in a leaked exam papers scandal that has sparked mass student protests. His promise came a day after thousands of protesters, led by the social media-driven Cockroach Janta Party, demonstrated in New Delhi, sparking fresh clashes with police. The snowballing protests have become one of the biggest challenges to Modi since his re-election for a third term in office in 2024.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: 'Mykhailo Fedorov was fired for his successes in fighting corruption in the defense sector'
articles.summary: François Picard is pleased to welcome Daria Kaleniuk, Executive Director of the Anti-corruption Action Centre. Ukraine's wartime challenge is no longer only military, but institutional. Ms. Kaleniuk contends that battlefield success and democratic resilience are inseparable from deep reform of the defence establishment. While welcoming President Zelensky's replacement of the commander-in-chief with a younger, reform-oriented military leader, she argues that this represents only "half" of the necessary changes. The more consequential battle, in her view, concerns governance.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: 'Cockroach Janta Party' takes India by storm
articles.summary: Born from a satirical retort to a passing comment by India's top judge, the "Cockroach Janta Party" has grown into a full-fledged movement protesting the government's mishandling of the nationwide medical entrance examination in May. Despite a violent crackdown on a peaceful march heading to the Indian parliament in New Delhi on Monday, members of the movement have kept up their protest. FRANCE 24 explains how the CJP came to be.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India: Youth-led 'Cockroach' protests increase pressure on Modi's government
articles.summary: With each passing day, India's youth-led cockroach movement seems to swell. As the sit-in by anti-corruption campaigners grows in New Delhi, opposition lawmakers relay their call for the education minister to resign over the leaking of exam tests. The standoff grew with the Supreme Court refusing to hear a police brutality petition launched after Monday's crackdown on those trying to reach parliament. Details from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in New Delhi, Sarah Jacob.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Indian students vow to continue 'cockroach movement' protests despite crackdown
articles.summary: Protests continue for a third day in the Indian capital, New Delhi, as pressure mounts on Narendra Modi to sack his education minister. The youth-led movement remains defiant even after Monday's heavy handed police crackdown. While the minister in question says the government remains committed to reform, the so-called Cockroach party say he's incompetent, and they want him out. Details by Delano D'Souza.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India's Cockroach protests vow to continue despite police crackdown
articles.summary: The leaders of India's youth-led Cockroach movement are vowing to continue protesting a day after police cracked down on demonstrators.
