They have been demanding the country's education minister, Dharmendra Pradhan, resign amid repeated leaks for entrance tests to medical schools. While two of the movement's members met with a government minister on July 20th, India's prime minister, Narendra Modi, is failing to address the issue for now. Delano D'Souza reports.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: India's opposition leader calls for Modi to step down as youth-led 'Cockroach' protests press on
articles.summary: Rahul Gandhi, India's opposition leader, called for Prime Minister Narendra Modi to resign on Tuesday "for destroying the future" of the country's youth. The youth-led Cockroach movement continued their protests in New Delhi, refusing to leave their sit-in site a day after police used tear has and batons to disperse demonstrators marching towards parliament.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Beijing summons Philippine ambassador over clash in disputed South China Sea shoal
articles.summary: Beijing and Manila summoned each other's ambassadors Tuesday following a confrontation between Chinese and Philippine sailors at a disputed shoal in the South China Sea. China continues to claim sovereignty over almost the entirety of the global trade route.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Indian police baton-charge 'Cockroach Party' protesters marching to parliament
articles.summary: Armoured riot police charged demonstrators taking part in a banned march on parliament in India's capital New Delhi on Monday linked to growing anger over irregularities in major university examinations. Saurav ‌Das, a spokesperson for the satirical Cockroach Janta Party, said that two members of the movement were on their way to meet a senior minister in Prime Minister Narendra Modi's cabinet.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: India bans march on parliament by ‘Cockroach’ activists, risking a standoff
articles.summary: Police in New Delhi on Sunday banned a planned march on the Indian parliament by supporters of the viral, opposition Cockroach Janata Party. The demonstration set for Monday, the start of parliament's monsoonsession, follows growing calls for the education minister's resignation over exam paper leaks and the forced removal of a hunger-striking activist to hospital.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Indian police shift Cockroach Party activist on hunger strike to hospital against his wish
articles.summary: Indian police on Saturday forcibly moved environmentalist Sonam Wangchuk to hospital after his health deteriorated during a weeks-long hunger strike in New Delhi. Wangchuk, a prominent activist tied to the viral, opposition Cockroach Janata Party, is seeking education reforms. His family has denounced the “lack of transparency" and trust in Indian authorities.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Japan changes imperial succession law but keeps ban on female emperor
articles.summary: Japan's parliament on Friday enacted changes to imperial succession rules, allowing male distant relatives to rejoin the imperial family and women to retain royal status after marrying commoners. The legislation, however, keeps the ban on female emperors despite opinion polls showing broad public support for allowing women to ascend the Chrysanthemum Throne.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: China's Xi urges global cooperation on AI, warns against single-country dominance
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping said on Friday artificial intelligence should not be dominated by any single country, calling for greater international cooperation on AI development and governance at a major conference in Shanghai. His remarks come as Chinese AI firms challenge US rivals and concerns grow over AI's military, cyber and terrorist misuse.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Japan: Growing number of young workers revive culture of corporate machismo
articles.summary: In Japan, a new generation of office workers is reviving a bygone corporate culture. Around the world, Gen-Z has garnered a reputation as delicate, even reticent employees. A growing cohort of young Japanese salarymen - and women - are embracing a work culture some are calling "corporate machismo" - a hard-charging, zealous approach to business that some see as the key to the country's post-World War 2 economic boom.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: China's economic growth slows to weakest pace in over three years
articles.summary: Economic reports on Wednesday found that Chinese growth has sunk to the slowest pace in over three years. Despite benefitting from the global AI boom, the country has not managed to offset the slump due to a struggling property sector, drop in domestic spending and trade disruptions caused by the war in Iran.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Andy Burnham's promise to deliver tangible improvements to Britons' lives put to the test
articles.summary: Former Greater Manchester mayor Andy Burnham is set to become the United Kingdom's new Prime Minister this Monday. He will do so having reiterated a commitment to help raise the standard of living in the country. However, the Labour leader's agenda will be tested by the country's financial situation and his prior commitments, both of which will limit the scope of his plans. In this segment, we'll look at how his policies promise to deliver higher growth in the short and long term.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: US imposes a 25 percent tariff on some Brazilian imports, citing unfair trade practices
articles.summary: The United States will slap 25 percent tariffs on some Brazilian goods starting July 22 following a yearlong investigation under the Trade Act of 1974. The probe concluded that Brazil engaged in unfair trade practices. Brazilian President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva condemned the move, saying it was politically motivated to favour his rival for upcoming elections, Flavio Bolsonaro. Also in this edition, we look at the Japanese firm trying to bring back 1980's style corporate culture.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: Chinese growth in second quarter weakest since Covid-19 era
articles.summary: Official data released on Wednesday shows China's GDP grew 4.3 percent in the second quarter, compared to a year prior. The last time quarterly growth was that weak was in late 2022, when China was feeling the impact of the Covid-19 pandemic. Slow consumer demand, despite a surge in exports, helps explain the slowdown. Also in this edition, Gibraltar's business community breathes a sigh of relief as the physical border between the British overseas territory and Spain is removed.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: Ukraine strikes halt shipping on key wheat route as Russian fuel crisis deepens
articles.summary: Ukrainian drone strikes have brought shipping in the Sea of Azov to a near standstill, disrupting a corridor that carries up to a quarter of Russia's wheat exports and sending tremors through global grain and oil markets. They have also knocked out a significant share of Russia's refining capacity, prompting Moscow to ban diesel exports until the end of July and further unsettling global oil markets. In Russian-occupied Crimea, petrol prices have reached a record high.
articles.author: Charlotte Lam

articles.title: How heatwaves are changing France's real-estate market
articles.summary: Crude oil prices surge as renewed US-Iran strikes fuel market fears. In France, real-estate agents say property buyers are changing priorities as heatwaves become more frequent. And Cuba suffers another nationwide blackout amid the impact of US sanctions.
articles.author: Bryan QUINN

articles.title: Nike and Adidas locked in World Cup standoff as tournament heats up
articles.summary: As the World Cup quarterfinals get under way, the race to number one between Nike and Adidas heats up. India and Australia sign a new uranium deal. And, OpenAI rolls out its newest model GPT-5.6 Sol to the general public.
articles.author: Camille KNIGHT

articles.title: UniCredit closes in on Commerzbank takeover
articles.summary: Italy's second biggest bank, Unicredit, is closing in on a takeover of Germany's second biggest bank Commerzbank after saying it secured 47.6% of the lender's shares on Wednesday. The move is facing widespread opposition in Germany, notably from the federal government, which has a 12% stake in the company. Also, new "freedom fuel" filling stations are appearing across the United States, offering cheaper petrol and receiving strong backing from the White House.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: IMF lowers 2026 global growth forecast to 3% but projects rebound in 2027
articles.summary: The IMF has cut its global growth forecast for the second time this year, flagging "uncertainty and risks" brought on by the war in Iran. Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez responds to threats from Donald Trump that the US will cut off all trade with his country. And, the heatwave is putting France's power system under pressure.
articles.author: Camille KNIGHT

articles.title: US revokes waiver for Iranian oil sales amid renewed Gulf strikes
articles.summary: The US Treasury Department has announced it will no longer allow Iranian oil sales to be conducted in US dollars on global markets after several tankers were hit by projectiles while attempting to cross the Strait of Hormuz. The move has left more than 60 million barrels of Iranian crude stranded at sea without any clear buyers. Also in this edition, we go inside a Chinese air conditioning factory racing to meet soaring European demand as heatwaves drive up sales.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: Undeterred by blasts, Macron says France ready to help rebuild Syria's economy
articles.summary: French President Emmanuel Macron said Tuesday that France is ready to help rebuild Syria's economy and banking sector, as he continued his Damascus visit undeterred by two bomb blasts near the hotel he was staying in.
articles.author: Charlotte Lam

articles.title: Samsung Electronics profits surge 1,800% annually amid artificial intelligence spending boom
articles.summary: South Korean chipmaker Samsung Electronics posted record quarterly profits Tuesday thanks to the global AI infrastructure buildout coupled with a memory chip shortage. Also in this edition, oil futures rise as tensions reignite in the Hormuz Strait and Canada commits to its biggest-ever defence contract. Finally, Cuba experiences its third nationwide blackout of the year as its fuel reserves dwindle.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: OPEC raises output but cartel's future remains unsure
articles.summary: A handful of OPEC+ countries have agreed to increase their output targets from August, but the cartel is fighting for its survival after the UAE's departure. Also, A French company is using the River Seine to cool down Paris's buildings. Finally, Sky says it's buying ITV's broadcast channels and streaming service for £1.6bn.
articles.author: Camille KNIGHT

articles.title: Earthquake damage threatens Venezuela's beach tourism centers
articles.summary: The earthquakes that hit Venezuela in late June have devastated seaside towns where tourism has been a vital economic lifeline for an already struggling population. Also, tanker traffic picks up through the Strait of Hormuz, and Europe seeks to convince the US that it's boosting defence spending.
articles.author: Bryan QUINN

articles.title: Why Anthropic won't mind Alibaba's Claude ban
articles.summary: Chinese tech giant Alibaba has ordered staff to stop using Anthropic's Claude Code after the US coding tool was found to be flagging users’ connecting from China. But Anthropic is already trying to stop Chinese firms from using Claude at all and accuses Alibaba of running large "distillation" campaigns against it, saying that the Chinese giant created around 25,000 fake accounts to train its own models on the US AI programme.
articles.author: Peter O'BRIEN

articles.title: German reforms, Google's final EU defeat and a $20M Swift wedding?
articles.summary: In today’s edition, FRANCE 24's Charlotte Lam takes a look at Germany’s new tax and pension reforms, Google’s big loss in EU courts and the “Swiftonomics” bonanza that the star’s wedding could bring to New York City.
articles.author: Charlotte Lam

articles.title: Andy Burnham outlines his vision for UK economy with promise to raise living standards
articles.summary: Andy Burnham, the former mayor of Greater Manchester, is likely to be the next British prime minister following Keir Starmer's resignation. Central to Burnham's platform is improving living standards that have stagnated or even fallen since the 2008 global financial crisis. But with weak public finances, how realistic is his plan? FRANCE 24's Charles Pellegrin talks to Renaud Foucart, senior lecturer in economics at Lancaster University.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: EU top court rejects Google's appeal against record €4.1 billion antitrust fine
articles.summary: The European Court of Justice on Thursday dismissed Google's appeal against a record fine imposed by EU antitrust regulators eight years ago for using its Android operating system to block rivals, in a ruling likely to boost Europe's crackdown on Big Tech.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Why Anthropic's most powerful AI models are back online
articles.summary: Anthropic's Mythos 5 and Fable 5 are back online this Wednesday after the company said it had productive conversations with the US government. Also, Kevin Warsh makes his first public appearance as Federal Reserve chairman. Plus shares of Meta rise after news that the company is building out a new cloud business.
articles.author: Camille KNIGHT

articles.title: Trump made over $1 billion thanks to crypto in 2025
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump made over a billion dollars with various crypto-related ventures in 2025, according to his annual financial disclosure report. The earnings, coming from royalties tied to the Trump memecoin and token sales from crypto firm World Liberty Financial, have prompted accusations of conflicts of interest from watchdog groups. Also in this edition: the US commerce department lifts its export ban on Anthropic's latest AI models.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: UK government likely to challenge Paramount takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery
articles.summary: The British government says it could step in to challenge Paramount Skydance's $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros Discovery. Also, French inflation slowed to just 1.8 percent in June year-on-year, down from 2.4 percent in May. Plus, more than 1 million undocumented people in Spain apply to obtain legal status as part of an economic bet that immigration is what's keeping the country's growth alive.
articles.author: Camille KNIGHT

articles.title: French heatwave threatens food inflation as agriculture sector suffers
articles.summary: Tomatoes cook on the vine and cereal crops get scorched – climate change is hitting French agriculture, and shoppers are poised to bear the brunt of it. Also, the EU and China set an October deadline to make progress on trade disputes, while the ECB Chief Christine Lagarde says the Eurozone economy is resilient enough to withstand an end to exceptional monetary policy measures.
articles.author: Bryan QUINN

articles.title: South Korea bets big on AI with nearly a trillion dollars in investment
articles.summary: South Korea bets big on artificial intelligence with nearly $1 trillion worth of investment through 2029. Also in this edition, Comcast announces it will spin off NBCUniversal into a separate, publicly traded company. Plus France takes aim at Shein, Temu and AliExpress with a new law aimed at curbing ultra-fast fashion.
articles.author: Camille KNIGHT

articles.title: China, EU commerce ministers meet amid widening trade imbalance
articles.summary: EU Trade Commissioner Maros Sefcovic and his Chinese counterpart are meeting in Brussels as Europe prepares countermeasures to battle a flood of cheap imports. Also, oil prices climb after a weekend of renewed strikes between the US and Iran, and South Korea unveils a massive new investment in chip production.
articles.author: Bryan QUINN

articles.title: VivaTech 2026: Space race hits new heights with reusable technology
articles.summary: Space loomed large over the 2026 VivaTech festival. Startups and technology giants alike have entered the new space economy – a sector previously dominated by government agencies. FRANCE 24’s Business Editor Kate Moody sat down with Marta Oliveira, Co-founder and Chief Operations Officer at Atmos Space Cargo, to talk about reusable rockets, raising money in the private sector and international competition in the 21st century space race.
articles.author: Kate MOODY

articles.title: Maritime traffic picks up in Strait of Hormuz, but uncertainty lingers
articles.summary: Oil prices continue their slide on Thursday as traffic through the Hormuz Strait has picked up over the past few days. Uncertainty lingers for the shipping industry, though, as disagreements over a potential toll to pass through the Strait could be a stumbling block in US-Iran talks. Also in this edition, US chipmaker Micron's better-than-expected sales forecast sends AI stocks surging again.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: Power outages and melting roads: Heatwave strains French infrastructure
articles.summary: Power outages, train delays, and melting roads – the current heatwave is straining France's infrastructure. Electricity provider EDF says it has had to reduce its nuclear power output, but that it still has enough capacity to meet demand. Also in the show: the UN's International Maritime Organization starts evacuating some of the 11,000 sailors stranded in the Strait of Hormuz, and Europe's defence industry prepares for a boost with the IPO of Franco-German tank maker KNDS.
articles.author: Kate MOODY

articles.title: Massive AI spending and higher interest rates: What's behind the tech sell-off?
articles.summary: Tech stocks around the world fell on Tuesday, with the flagship Nasdaq index closing 2.2 percent down at the end of the session. In this edition, we look at how markets reacted this Wednesday and some of the reasons why investors sold their shares: massive projected capital expenditure on AI, as well as the prospect of higher interest rates. Also, we examine Spain's pioneering climate leave policy.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: World risks 'losing control of technology' without AI governance, Chinese PM warns
articles.summary: Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Wednesday warned of "serious consequences" if governments fail to step up regulation of artificial intelligence as he addressed the World Economic Forum in Dalian known as the "summer Davos".
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: UN chief calls on AI firms to 'come clean' on environmental costs
articles.summary: As Europe swelters under a major heatwave, the high energy consumption of artificial intelligence has come into the spotlight. At a climate conference in London, UN Secretary General Antonio Guterres called on AI companies to disclose the environmental impact of their systems. Plus, Iran rejects the US’s claim that any potentially unfrozen Iranian assets would be controlled by the US and Qatar and used exclusively to buy American food and medicine.
articles.author: Yuka ROYER

articles.title: US waives Iran oil sanctions as part of 60-day peace negotiations
articles.summary: The United States temporarily waived sanctions on Iranian oil exports on Monday, opening the door for Tehran to return to global energy markets as negotiations between the two countries continue. In this edition, we look at the impact this has had on oil prices, while also examining major job cuts at Oracle linked to AI-driven restructuring and a sharp sell-off in technology stocks that's rippled from Wall Street to Asian and European markets.
articles.author: Charles PELLEGRIN

articles.title: Pogacar closes in on Tour de France victory, Carapaz wins Queen stage
articles.summary: Tadej Pogacar is set to join cycling's all-time greats after all but sealing a record-equalling fifth Tour de France title on Saturday as Ecuadorian Richard Carapaz won the 20th stage on Alpe d'Huez.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Football: Germany unveils new head coach with eyes on 2030 World Cup
articles.summary: The international coaching carousel is in full swing. Jurgen Klopp was officially unveiled as Germany head coach on Friday, tasked with reviving a national team that has struggled to recapture the heights of its 2014 World Cup triumph. Italy have also turned to a legend, appointing 2006 World Cup winner Andrea Pirlo to lead the Azzurri as they look to end years of disappointment on the global stage. And in France, Zinedine Zidane is expected to be named Les Bleus' new head coach on Tuesday.
articles.author: L'Equipe TV

articles.title: Pogacar takes Tour de France stage 19 with solo attack on Alpe d'Huez
articles.summary: Slovenia's four-time champion Tadej Pogacar on Friday further consolidated his overall lead by taking stage 19 of the Tour de France. He made the punishing climb up the Alpe d'Huez in 35 minutes and 27 seconds.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Ecuadorian Richard Carapaz wins Stage 18 in a solo breakaway
articles.summary: Following a decisive attack in the closing stages, Richard Carapaz claimed victory on Stage 18, leaving all his rivals trailing in his wake. He finished ahead of Switzerland’s Mauro Schmid and the American Matteo Jorgenson, who crossed the line 45 seconds behind him. Today, the riders face another mountain stage, with over 3,000 metres of elevation gain.
articles.author: L'Equipe TV

articles.title: Ecuador’s Carapaz wins Tour de France stage 18, Pogacar loses key climbing teammate
articles.summary: Ecuador's ​Richard Carapaz scored a decisive win of the Tour de France at stage 18 on Thursday, securing victory in the final climb to Orcieres-Merlette. While Tadej Pogacar had previously maintained his overall lead, the Slovenian suffered a blow as key teammate Brandon McNulty abandoned the race.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: France expected to name football legend Zinedine Zidane as Les Bleus' new coach
articles.summary: The French Football Federation on Thursday said it would unveil France's new coach at a news conference on Tuesday, July 28. Football legend Zinedine Zidane is widely expected to replace Didier Deschamps as the national team's new coach.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Mountain biker becomes first to ride off a hot air balloon
articles.summary: You might want to look away from this next story if you're afraid of heights. A young Austrian mountain biker has performed a world first - by riding off a hot air balloon on his bike. Don't worry, both had parachutes attached to them. The trick, which took place in Bulgaria, took two years to prepare.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Zinedine Zidane to be officially appointed as France manager on Tuesday
articles.summary: A new era will begin on Tuesday for 'Les Bleus'. Zinedine Zidane is expected to be officially appointed as the head coach of the French national team on Tuesday. The 54-year-old coach will sign a four-year contract, until the 2030 World Cup. He will bring an end to the Didier Deschamps era, who has been in charge of Les Bleus since 2012.
articles.author: L'Equipe TV

articles.title: Philipsen wins Tour de France 17th stage as Pogacar retains overall lead
articles.summary: Belgium's Jasper Philipsen won the 17th stage of the 2026 Tour de France on Wednesday with a comfortable lead ahead of Mauro Schmid and Olav Kooij at the end of the Alpine stage. While Tadej Pogacar struggled throughout the stage after suffering from a stomach problem the previous night, the Slovenian cyclist remains in the lead.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Tour de France: Evenepoel wins time trial to strengthen second overall
articles.summary: Remco Evenepoel won the individual time trial on Stage 16 of the Tour de France, 2 days after his victory at Plateau de Solaison. The three-time world time trial champion finished 28 seconds ahead of Tadej Pogacar and 1'04'' clear of Mattias Skjelmose, between Évian and Thonon. The Belgian remains second overall, 4'32'' behind the Slovenian in the yellow jersey.
articles.author: L'Equipe TV

articles.title: Evenepoel beats Pogacar by seconds in stage 16 of Tour de France
articles.summary: Olympic champion Remco Evenepoel powered to victory in the Tour de France's stage 16 time trial on Tuesday, beating overall leader Tadej Pogacar by 28 seconds to trim the Slovenian's advantage.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Fake images circulate of Spanish World Cup players draped in Palestinian flags
articles.summary: An image generated by artificial intelligence shows Spanish footballer Lamine Yamal celebrating his World Cup win while draped in a Palestinian flag. People have also been circulating an image of player Pedro Porro, who they falsely claim is wearing a Palestinian flag around his waist.
articles.author: The FRANCE 24 Observers

articles.title: World Cup 2026: Spain return to Madrid in triumph
articles.summary: Spain reunited with their supporters in Madrid less than 24 hours after winning the World Cup final against Argentina (1-0, after extra time). The players of La Roja, alongside head coach Luis de la Fuente, displayed the trophy upon their arrival at the airport before taking part in celebrations across the capital. More than 1 million people attended the parade, which ended with a major concert at Cibeles Square.
articles.author: L'Equipe TV

articles.title: World Cup 2026: for New York souvenir shops, the impact is mixed
articles.summary: The 2026 World Cup is over. And for New York’s souvenir shops, the impact is mixed.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: ⚽World Cup 2026: Donald Trump tries to steal the spotlight from Spain
articles.summary: 🏆🇪🇸 After Spain’s World Cup 2026 victory over #Argentina, Donald Trump appeared determined to stay in the spotlight during the trophy presentation, with #FIFA President Gianni #Infantino stepping in so the champions could take centre stage. 🎤
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: 'We gave it everything': Fans react to World Cup final game
articles.summary: From Madrid to Barcelona, Spanish fans were out in full force to celebrate their team's win. It took 11 shots to get them the 1-0 victory over Argentina. Meanwhile, in Buenos Aires, fans still celebrated late into the night, despite coming in second place for Lionel Messi's last World Cup outing.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: 'Absolute joy spilling out' for Spain's 'new golden generation' of football
articles.summary: By winning the World Cup final against Argentina, Spain has become the first country to hold the men's and the women's title at the same time. The men's team is now at 38 consecutive successful games, a record. Now, Madrid is preparing for the celebrations that will mark the return of La Roja to its home. FRANCE 24's Sarah Morris tells us more on the atmosphere in Madrid.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Spain's World Cup heroes celebrate with victory parade through Madrid
articles.summary: Spain's World Cup-winning team returned home on Monday for a royal reception by King Felipe VI ahead of an open-top bus parade through central Madrid. La Roja beat Argentina in the final on Sunday to clinch their second World Cup title after an extra-time goal by Ferran Torres.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Spain beat Argentina to win World Cup for second time
articles.summary: Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time in the World Cup final. The Spanish have been crowned champions for the second time in their history. Ferran Torres scored the only goal of the match.
articles.author: L'Equipe TV

articles.title: World Cup 2026: Spanish fans celebrate their team's victory in New York
articles.summary: As Spain were crowned champions after extra-time thriller against Argentina, fans in New York celebrated the second World Cup title for La Roja.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Trump says World Cup made US a 'soccer country' as he presents trophy to Spain
articles.summary: President Donald Trump presented Spain with the World Cup 2026 trophy after its victory over Argentina on Sunday, declaring the tournament showed that the United States had become "a soccer country". The final capped more than a year of logistical planning by US, Canadian and Mexican hosts amid controversy over US immigration restrictions on some fans.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Spain win World Cup by beating Argentina 1-0
articles.summary: La Roja have been crowned World Champions for the second time after a tense battle with Argentina in New Jersey. Spain’s Ferran Torres managed to fire a shot past Emiliano Martinez in extra time as he scored the only goal of the game. At the time, Argentina was playing with 10 players, as Enzo Fernandez was sent off after picking up a second yellow card. FRANCE 24's team analyses the game and the tournament after a record 104 matches.
articles.author: James VASINA

articles.title: Messi denied dream farewell as Argentina lose World Cup final to Spain
articles.summary: Argentina's 1-0 loss to Spain in the 2026 World Cup final on Sunday brought star forward Lionel Messi's dream of winning back-to-back trophies crashing down to earth.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: World Cup 2026: Spain crowned champions after extra-time thriller against Argentina
articles.summary: Spain were crowned world champions for the second time in their history on Sunday, defeating defending champions Argentina 1-0 after extra time at MetLife Stadium in New Jersey. Ferran Torres' decisive strike in extra time settled a tightly contested final, giving Luis de la Fuente's Roja their second World Cup title, sixteen years after their first in 2010, and completing a historic Euro-World Cup double.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: The Bayeux Tapestry in London: 'A diplomatic operation that almost never happened'
articles.summary: Nearly 1,000 years after chronicling the Norman conquest of England, the Bayeux Tapestry is making history once again. The fragile 11th-century embroidery has arrived in London on an unprecedented loan to the British Museum, prompting delight and concern in equal measure. Celebrated as one of Europe''s greatest medieval treasures, its journey has reignited debates over heritage, diplomacy and the risks of moving delicate cultural artefacts.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: UNESCO places ancient Lebanese city of Tyre on heritage danger list
articles.summary: UNESCO on Wednesday added Tyre, an ancient coastal city in southern Lebanon founded by the Phoenicians, to its list of world heritage sites in danger following months of Israeli bombardment. Founded around 4,700 years ago, Tyre is home to archaeological treasures including two protected UNESCO areas.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Louvre heist: 'We've recovered millions worth of artworks thanks to tipsters', explains legal expert
articles.summary: Annette Young is pleased to welcome Christopher Marinello, veteran lawyer, founder of Art Recovery International and one of the world's foremost experts in recovering stolen, looted, and missing works of art. The reopening of the Apollo Gallery at the Louvre, nine months after one of the most brazen museum thefts in recent history, marks more than the restoration of a famous exhibition space. It exposes a broader tension between public access to cultural heritage and the growing vulnerability of museums in an era of increasingly sophisticated organised crime.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: D. Rykner says the Louvre needs to be 'refurbished', Macron's big project is 'useless and expensive'
articles.summary: Stuart Norval is pleased to welcome Didier Rykner, Art Historian, Investigative Journalist and Founder / Editor in Chief of La Tribune de l’Art. Offering a forceful critique of the Louvre's priorities, Rykner argues that the museum's challenge is not a lack of resources, rather a misallocation of them. While acknowledging that security is a both necessary and inevitable expense, he contends that the greater threat to the Louvre lies in the deterioration of its historic fabric and the diversion of funding towards what he regards as an unnecessary, politically driven architectural expansion.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: 'France wants to lead the way' with under-15s social media ban
articles.summary: French lawmakers are expected to pass a bill on July 21st banning social media access to children under 15. If approved, France would follow Australia's lead, where the world's first ban ​for under-16s ‌on platforms including Facebook, Snapchat, TikTok and YouTube came into ⁠force in December, as concerns grow over the impact social media has on the health and safety of minors.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: BTS storms Paris: K-pop phenomenon plays stade de France
articles.summary: The Korean superstar boyband is wrapping up the European leg of their Arirang album tour in the French capital before dates in North and South America. FRANCE 24 takes a look at the K-pop phenomenon’s meteoric rise.
articles.author: Olivia SALAZAR-WINSPEAR

articles.title: Ali Zalzali’s shows gothic glamour in his début couture collection
articles.summary: His blossoming, botanical and flowing forms recall the life cycles of plants and humans. Designer Ali Zalzali tells FRANCE 24 about creating his first couture collection, ‘Natura Morta’ and the evocative short film he made to conjure up the universe of these hand-crafted pieces.
articles.author: Olivia SALAZAR-WINSPEAR

articles.title: The Odyssey: Matt Damon, Lupita Nyong’o, Anne Hathaway relive the epic
articles.summary: In this edition, Critic Emma Jones tells us why Christopher Nolan’s take on the Greek epic was worth the wait – and the eye-watering budget – and how the themes of this ancient story still speak to contemporary audiences. The all-star cast includes Matt Damon as a world-weary Odysseus, Anne Hathaway embodies a very patient Penelope and Lupita Nyong’O plays both Helen of Troy and her twin sister Clytemnestra.
articles.author: Olivia SALAZAR-WINSPEAR

articles.title: Ahmed El Attar brings rage, resistance and humanity to the stage in Avignon
articles.summary: In this edition, arts24 decamps to the south of France for a special show from the world-renowned Avignon theatre festival as it celebrates its 80th edition. Korean is this year’s guest language at the event, offering audiences an insight into drama, dance and literary work from Korean artists. We also check out Julien Gosselin’s high-tech, literary exploration of evil in ‘Maldoror’, on stage at the Palais des Papes and talk to Egyptian director Ahmed El Attar about his recent work.
articles.author: Olivia SALAZAR-WINSPEAR

articles.title: Jurassic Park, The Piano, The Tudors... New Zealand actor Sam Neill dies at 78
articles.summary: New Zealand actor Sam Neill, known for his roles in "Jurassic Park" and "The Piano", has died aged 78. Neill had announced in April that he was cancer-free after undergoing treatment for stage-three ​blood cancer. Tributes are flowing in for the star, including from New Zealand Prime Minister Christopher Luxon who said Neill was "one of the greats". Story by Carys Garland.
articles.author: FRANCE24

articles.title: Summer soundtrack: Charli XCX and the return of The Strokes
articles.summary: On today's Arts24 music show, Jennifer Ben Brahim brings us a roundup of upcoming album releases to add to your summer playlists. From the return of indie sleaze icons The Strokes, who are set to release their first album in six years, "Reality Awaits", to a British pop star hoping to recreate the success of her 2024 record Brat – the album that sparked the viral internet trend dubbed "Brat Summer". Her seventh album, Music, Fashion, Film, features musician John Cale, designer Marc Jacobs and filmmaker Martin Scorsese on the cover. Here's the single "Wink Wink".
articles.author: Jennifer BEN BRAHIM

articles.title: Actor Sam Neill, star of 'Jurassic Park', dies at 78
articles.summary: New Zealand actor Sam Neill, best known for his roles in "Jurassic Park" and "The Piano', died Monday at the age of 78, according to a statement from his family on social media.
articles.author: FRANCE 24

articles.title: Cardi B, Teyana Taylor and Bad Bunny brave Paris heat
articles.summary: Paris has been hosting its autumn-winter couture collections amid simmering temperatures, with celebrities sporting parasols and fans as they watch the shows. Fashion journalist Alice Pfeiffer tells us why "Blazymania" has taken hold, as Chanel's new artistic director continues his winning streak with designs inspired by Coco Chanel herself. At Dior, Jonathan Anderson presents an accessible, floral collection, while Pierpaolo Piccioli draws stars including Cynthia Erivo, Demi Moore and Teyana Taylor to the front row for his Balenciaga debut.
articles.author: Olivia SALAZAR-WINSPEAR

articles.title: A cultural stroll through Paris with Kalash and Manon Lisa
articles.summary: A summer of music with Paris des Arts! On today's show, we meet up with French rapper Kalash as well as singer Manon Lisa.
articles.author: Valérie FAYOLLE
